# Interactive Resources — A-Level Music Technology

> Interactive learning tools for A-Level Music Technology (Pearson Edexcel Component 4) covering synthesis, EQ, compression, audio numeracy, and more.

Built by Mike Lehnert. Deployed at https://interactive-resources-eight.vercel.app

## What This App Does

A collection of interactive, browser-based tools that let students explore music technology concepts through direct manipulation. Each tool is designed around a specific curriculum topic and uses the Web Audio API for real-time audio processing.

### Available Tools

- **Synth Explorer** — Interactive synthesis with oscillator controls, ADSR envelopes, and waveform visualisation
- **EQ Trainer** — Hands-on equalisation with frequency bands and real-time audio feedback
- **Compressor Tool** — Dynamic processing with threshold, ratio, attack, and release controls
- **Octave Period Trainer** — Numeracy tool for calculating frequency, period, and octave relationships (Topic 2.5)
- **Revision Quizzes** — Topic-based self-assessment with spaced repetition support
- Additional tools covering delay, sampling, automation, and signal flow

### How Students Use It

- Browse by curriculum topic
- Interact with audio parameters in real time
- Self-assess understanding through built-in quizzes
- Use as a revision resource alongside classroom teaching

## Curriculum Alignment

All resources are mapped to the Pearson Edexcel Level 3 Advanced GCE in Music Technology, Component 4: Producing and Analysing. Curriculum section numbers (e.g., 1.11 EQ, 1.3 Synthesis, 1.9 Dynamic Processing) are used throughout.

## Tech Stack

Next.js, React, Web Audio API, Tailwind CSS, Vercel

## Important Context

- Designed for UK A-Level students aged 16-18
- All audio processing happens in the browser — no server-side audio
- Resources are pedagogically structured with progressive difficulty
- Interactive elements follow dual coding principles (visual + audio feedback)

## Not Intended For

- General music production tutorials
- Professional audio engineering reference
- DAW-specific instruction (though Ableton Live 12 is used in classroom context)
